chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr and ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If you come to the well while you are junub and do not find a bucket nor anything with which to draw water, then perform tayammum with the earth, for the Lord of the water and the Lord of the earth is One. And do not fall into the well, and do not spoil the people’s water for them.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well serving as the water source
key_terms.بِالصَّعِيدِ: with the earth or earthly surface used for tayammum
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.دَلْوًا: a bucket used to draw water
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمْ: then perform tayammum as the prescribed dry ablution
key_terms.مَاءَهُمْ: their water, meaning the community’s usable water

ai.seo_question: What should a junub person do if water is present in a well but there is no bucket to draw it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person in janabah who reaches a well or water source but has no means to draw water. In that case, he is instructed to perform tayammum, while also avoiding contaminating or ruining the water used by others, combining ritual law with consideration for communal rights.
